inputs.sbc_source: 10-K FY2025 cash flow statement SBC add-back ($203M, 0.73% of revenue); 9M-2026 add-back $159M vs $153M a year earlier (Q3 2026 10-Q), so the 0.75% forward path is unchanged. No separate equity-award withholding-tax cash line is disclosed (RSU share issuance is reported net of shares withheld), so the add-back is used as-is; the understatement is expected to be minor for an industrial.
inputs.wacc_rationale: 9.5%, UNCHANGED from the 2026-09-26 build, where it was built on a USD risk-free rate of ~4.2% (10yr UST) plus ~5.3pp ERP/beta premium for a cyclical industrial, already set toward the upper end of the house 8-11% US-industrial range in anticipation of the Chart debt. The observed post-close leverage (total debt $18.3B, net debt $14.2B, ~2.5x, S&P A-) is what that rate was set for, so no further premium is added: the extra debt is charged in full in the net-debt bridge, and the leverage/integration risk is charged in the scenario flows and the 25% bear weight (adaptations rule f: risk charged once). The risk-free rate was not re-fetched for this refresh. What would move it: loss of the A-category rating, or a move in the 10yr UST of more than ~50bp.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP filer: operating lease cost is already an operating expense inside adjusted EBITDA, so leases are charged once in the flows and operating lease liabilities are excluded from net debt (treatment B). No further adjustment.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are 100% consolidated; noncontrolling interests ($428M at 30 Sep 2026, of which $244M came with Chart) are deducted once, at book, in the equity bridge. The prior build made no NCI deduction.
inputs.notes: OWNER-FCF DCF (owner-fcf.md + owner-fcf-adaptations.md; cyclical US industrial, USD filer and quote). UPDATE of the 2026-09-26 build, not a rebuild; model unchanged. FY0 STAYS FY2025 (last complete fiscal year, revenue $27,733M, owner FCF $2,334M = reported FCF $2,537M less SBC $203M): there is no completed FY2026 to roll to, and the raised FY2026 guidance is booked as the year-1 driver outcome rather than as the compounding base. Chart enters through the growth path (stub in FY2026, full year in FY2027) and its cost through net debt. NET DEBT is now OBSERVED, replacing the prior build's estimate ($12,538M with synthetic debt/cash placeholders): Q3 2026 10-Q total debt $18,264M (short-term $788M + long-term $17,476M) less cash $4,068M = $14,196M. The 30 Sep 2026 balance sheet already contains nine months of FY2026 cash generation that the engine also counts inside year-1 FCF; against that the engine discounts every flow as if today were 31 Dec 2025, about 0.9 year too early. The two effects run in opposite directions and the second is the larger, so the convention is modestly conservative; neither is adjusted for, as in the prior build. INTEREST INCOME not stripped: the company is in net debt (9M-2026 interest income of $236M was inflated by pre-close acquisition cash and does not recur). BUYBACKS: none in 9M-2026 ($384M in FY2025); the flat share count is currently a modelling convention the company is not funding while it delevers toward <1.5x by H2 2028. TERMINAL CAP: base/bull 12x FCF (was 11x), bear 9x (unchanged). The prior note justified 11x by reference to OFSE's EV/EBITDA trading range, but the cap is a multiple of owner FCF, where 11x is roughly 5-6x EBITDA -- below any multiple BKR has traded at. 12x is the bottom of the house 12-15x band for cyclicals; Gordon at 9.5%/2.75% is ~15x, so THE CAP BINDS in base and bull (the prior note said it did not; it did). HORIZON 10 years, unchanged. RISK CHARGED ONCE: same 9.5% WACC in all three scenarios. D&A PATH deliberately unchanged at ~4.2-4.4% of revenue although reported D&A has stepped up (Q3 2026 $505M) -- the increase is purchase-accounting amortisation from a stock deal (goodwill stated as non-deductible), so it is not treated as a cash tax shield. CAPEX and WORKING-CAPITAL paths unchanged; note 9M-2026 working capital GENERATED $350M on progress collections, and the -8% capture is also applied to acquired revenue in FY2026-27, so both lean conservative.
inputs.share_count_date: 2026-09-30 (Q3 2026 10-Q: 992.7M Class A issued and outstanding; 998M weighted-average diluted for the quarter)
inputs.share_count_basis: 998M = Q3 2026 weighted-average diluted Class A shares from the 10-Q EPS note (basic issued 992.7M at 30 Sep 2026). Replaces the prior build's 1,005M gross-up estimate. Chart was an all-cash deal ($210/share), so no acquisition shares were issued. Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows -- charging both would double-count.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue_3yr_cagr, judgmentally preferred over equity_5yr_cagr and the reported/owner-FCF CAGRs
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR (0.83%) and owner-FCF CAGRs (50-81%) diverge enormously from revenue CAGRs (6-9%) and from each other. This is a cyclical-recovery artifact, not a real growth-rate signal: FY2020 was a COVID-driven trough (a $15.7B goodwill impairment crushed FY2020 equity and owner-FCF was only $120M that year on a 0.6% margin), so every CAGR anchored to 2020 or 2021 is inflated by the low base. EPS CAGRs are not computable cleanly because FY2020-2022 EPS was negative. Revenue CAGR is used as the primary anchor here instead of the house default (equity CAGR), because equity CAGR for a company that took a ~$16B one-off impairment mid-history is not a meaningful measure of underlying compounding -- the divergence is disclosed rather than silently resolved by picking equity CAGR by default.

base.narrative: FY2026 revenue lands at the midpoint of raised guidance ($29.2-30.1B, +6.9% on FY2025) at a 17.75% adjusted EBITDA margin (guide $5.13-5.4B). FY2027 grows ~10.5%, almost all of it mechanical: a full year of Chart (~$4.4B annualised vs a ~$2.0B stub) less the Waygate disposal (~$0.6B), with OFSE roughly flat as upstream spending improves only modestly and IET converting record backlog (RPO $39.4B) at a high-single-digit rate; management notes only about a third of gas-technology equipment backlog converts in 2027. FY2028 onward is the prior path, unchanged: 7% tapering to 2.75%. Margin rises from 17.75% to ~19.8% as IET aftermarket mix grows and Chart moves from ~17.6% toward its 22-23% target with $325M of cost synergies. Cash tax is re-based to 27% of EBIT falling to 25%: income taxes paid were $1,040M and $1,156M in FY2024-25 (about 32% of owner EBIT) and are guided to ~$1.0B for 2026 (about 27%), so the prior 21-23% path understated a structurally high cash tax burden from withholding taxes and unbenefited losses. Working capital stays at a -8% capture on revenue growth.

bull.narrative: FY2026 at the top of guidance; FY2027 +13% as IET converts faster on the >$50B Horizon 2 order outlook (LNG equipment approaching $10B, power systems approaching $15B, $4.9B of data-centre awards year to date) on top of the full-year Chart step-up. LNG turbomachinery share holds near 90% against Siemens Energy and Mitsubishi; Chart reaches its 22-23% margin target on schedule with commercial cross-sell on top of the $325M cost synergies; OFSE recovers with international and offshore spending into 2027-28. Later-year growth is the prior bull path, unchanged; margin reaches 22%; cash tax falls to 24% as the effective-rate programme delivers.

bear.narrative: FY2026 at the bottom of guidance; FY2027 grows only ~4% even with a full year of Chart, because OFSE falls as Saudi Aramco and other NOCs cut into an oil-price downcycle and AI/data-centre capex sentiment reverses, slowing power-systems orders and stretching backlog conversion. Siemens Energy and Mitsubishi take LNG share. Chart stalls near its current ~17.6% margin, the $325M of synergies slips, and with ~2.5x leverage the company has to prioritise debt paydown over buybacks while the A-category rating comes under further pressure. Growth stays at 2-2.5% thereafter (prior path, unchanged); group margin slips from 17.5% to ~16.2% and recovers only to 17%; cash tax stays at 27.5-28%; working capital capture is -12%.

scenario_narratives.base: Three-segment Baker Hughes (OFSE ~48% of revenue, IET ~41%, Chart ~11%) delivers raised FY2026 guidance, steps up ~10.5% in FY2027 on a full year of Chart net of the Waygate sale, then grows 7% tapering to 2.75% as record IET backlog converts; adjusted EBITDA margin rises from 17.75% to ~19.8% on IET aftermarket mix and Chart synergies, with cash tax at 27% easing to 25%.
scenario_narratives.bull: LNG turbomachinery dominance and data-centre power orders convert the >$50B Horizon 2 pipeline faster than guided, Chart hits its 22-23% margin target with cross-sell on top of cost synergies, and OFSE recovers with international and offshore spending -- low-double-digit growth in the middle years and a 22% margin.
scenario_narratives.bear: An oil-price downcycle and NOC capex cuts hit OFSE just as AI/data-centre capex sentiment reverses, turbomachinery share is lost to Siemens Energy and Mitsubishi, and Chart stalls near a 17.6% margin with synergies slipping -- all while carrying $14.2B of net debt at ~2.5x; growth is low-single-digit after FY2027 and margin compresses to ~16.2%.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: UNCHANGED at 25/50/25. Bear stays at 25% (house default 15%): OFSE cyclicality with NOC capex discipline still live, integration risk on a just-closed $14.2B cash acquisition, and leverage now observed at ~2.5x with an S&P downgrade to A- -- there is no covenant or refinancing pressure ($4.1B cash, nearest large maturity the $2.0B of two-year term loans), which is why it is not higher. Base 50%: FY2026 guidance was raised and backlog is at a record. Bull stays at 25% (default 35%) because it needs full Chart synergy capture, sustained LNG share and continued data-centre power orders to arrive together. What would move the weights: leverage tracking above the <1.5x-by-H2-2028 path, or a Chart margin that fails to progress from 17.6%, would raise the bear weight; the September rationale that the stock had re-rated ~40% no longer applies after the November sell-off, but price is not an input to scenario probabilities.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Baker Hughes is valued as a cyclical industrial on a strict owner-FCF DCF: SBC (about 0.75% of revenue) expensed with a flat share count, no interest-income strip because the company is in net debt, a 10-year horizon, one 9.5% WACC across scenarios, and a terminal value capped at 12x owner FCF (9x in the bear case), which binds. This refresh replaces the estimated post-Chart balance sheet with the observed one (net debt $14.2B at 30 Sep 2026) and re-bases three things on new evidence: the FY2026-27 revenue step from consolidating Chart, which the prior build carried the debt for but largely left out of revenue; the cash tax rate, re-based from 21-23% to 25-27% of EBIT on actual taxes paid; and the terminal cap, moved from 11x to the bottom of the house cyclical band. The model remains deliberately conservative against the market: the weighted value sits well below the share price, and the gap is mostly the terminal cap -- the market is capitalising the IET/Chart backlog at a multiple this model does not grant a business that still earns about half its EBITDA from oilfield services.
key_risks_to_valuation: Terminal cap binds in base and bull: each 1x of owner-FCF multiple is worth roughly the amount shown in the reconciliation bridge for the 11x-to-12x move, so the value is highly sensitive to a judgment, not a forecast
Leverage of ~2.5x after the Chart acquisition against a target of <1.5x by H2 2028; a downturn before deleveraging hits equity value disproportionately
Chart integration: margin must rise from ~17.6% to 22-23% and $325M of synergies ($70M executed) must be delivered; the $300M allowance for remaining cost-to-achieve cash is an estimate
OFSE oil-price cyclicality and NOC capex discipline; AI/data-centre power orders are the newest and least-tested leg of IET demand
Cash tax: taxes paid have run at 27-32% of owner EBIT; the base path assumes this eases to 25%, which management's effective-rate work has not yet shown in cash
Waygate proceeds ($1.45B gross, carried at $1.30B net) depend on a Q4 2026 close; Waygate's revenue (~$0.6B) and the tax leakage on the gain are estimates
Balance sheet is three months into FY2026 flows the engine also counts in year 1, offset by discounting from the start of FY2026 -- see inputs.notes
